status: requested; owner decision pending. This is a request, not a RAPP/1 trust anchor (§13.1), a rapp/1-registry, a §13 registry entry with authority, or a signature.
note: Machine-readable copy of ANCHOR-REQUEST.md. Only the estate owner can create the entries below, by signing the next revision of the registry of record. Everything in this repository is SYNTHETIC: fictional people and devices, signed with public test keys that anyone can re-derive. Real estate facts are cited by public pointer only; no real rappid is copied here (under RAPP/1 §13.1 a keyed rappid is a key fingerprint).

subject.finding: rapp_check at rapp-1@591e014 reports every signed frame under model/hive/streams/ as '§10 signature verification unavailable' (status unverified): the frames pass §7 steps 1-5, but no §13 registry lists their signers' keys.

trust_anchor.what: The estate owner's rappid (RAPP/1 §13.1), cited by public pointer. Its value is not copied into this repository.

requested.action: Append these entries, unchanged, to the registry of record in its next owner-signed revision (registry_seq 3 while the registry is at 2). Nothing else is requested.
requested.entry_type: spki (RAPP/1 §13.3; rapp_registry.ENTRY_MEMBERS['spki'] = type, rappid, spki_der_b64, deprecated)

self_consistency.what: Not trust. Each entry passes rapp_registry.validate_entry (its SPKI hashes to its rappid tail), and every frame's detached JWS verifies against its kid's entry with rapp.verify_detached_jws, both at rapp-1@591e014.
self_consistency.rederived_by: tests/test_model_hive.py (AnchorRequestTests), on every CI run, with the vendored reference

expected_after_ceremony.call: rapp_check.check_repo(<checkout>, signature_verifier=reg.signature_verifier()), with reg from rapp_registry.load_document(doc, entries_member='entries', trust_anchor=<estate_owner>)
expected_after_ceremony.checked_in_advance_with: an unsigned draft of that revision, which load_document reports only as 'draft' (never authority) and refuses without allow_unsigned; the draft was not kept
expected_after_ceremony.before_ceremony: persisted_seq=3 refuses today's registry_seq 2 as a rollback; with persisted_seq=2 the same check_repo call reports DRIFT with 17 x '§7 frame verification step 6' ('no spki entry for kid (registry absence is refusal)'), one for the first frame of each stream.
expected_after_ceremony.cli: The rapp_check command line supplies no signature verifier, so its verdict stays DRIFT (38 x '§10 signature verification unavailable', status unverified) even after the ceremony.

not_needed_for_rapp_check.note: rapp_check never calls rapp_registry.check_frame_binding and never reads genesis entries. Listed for completeness only; this request does not ask for them.

kind.why: RAPP/1 §7.2: a frame's kind family must be the §13 registry binding and match its stream_id form (rapp_registry.Registry.check_frame_binding). memory.save is already registered (family memory). hive2.* belong to the experimental frontier draft rapp-hive/2, and kinds are an estate-wide, append-only namespace, so registering them is an estate decision beyond this model.
kind.effect: A consumer that also runs check_frame_binding accepts 10 of the 38 frames (memory.save) with the six spki entries alone, and 38 of 38 with these kind entries added (checked with rapp_registry at rapp-1@591e014).

genesis.why: RAPP/1 §13.3: every stream registers its creation genesis; §7.6 heads descend from it. One entry per stream in model/hive/streams/.
genesis.effect: With these entries, each stream's seq-0 frame is its registered genesis (17 of 17).

sign_and_verify.needs: the cryptography package, and RAPP1_DIR naming a kody-w/rapp-1 checkout (591e014), whose rapp and rapp_registry it imports
sign_and_verify.verify: python3 tools/registry_sign.py verify --in ecosystem-spec.json --persisted-seq <last verified seq> --trust-anchor <estate_owner> (rapp_registry.load_document; refuses to run without an out-of-band trust anchor)
sign_and_verify.sign: python3 tools/registry_sign.py sign --key <estate owner key file> --in <next revision> --out ecosystem-spec.json

gate.run_by: bash .github/scripts/run-offline-gates.sh (workflows Drift lint and Standing guard), through .github/scripts/standing-guard.mjs local

steps: Fetch the registry of record from canonical_source and check it against the trust anchor: python3 tools/registry_sign.py verify --in ecosystem-spec.json --persisted-seq 2 --trust-anchor <estate_owner> must print 'verified: ok'.

Make the next revision: the same document without sig, registry_seq + 1, and requested.entries appended to 'entries' (append-only: every existing entry stays, unchanged and in order). Envelope members such as published_utc are the owner's to set.

The estate owner signs it: python3 tools/registry_sign.py sign --key <estate owner key file> --in <next revision> --out ecosystem-spec.json. The tool refuses a key path inside the repository and a key file that group or others can access ('key file must be mode 0600'), and refuses a key whose SPKI does not hash to the estate_owner rappid's tail. It signs canonical(document without sig) with a §10 detached JWS (EdDSA, kid = estate_owner), sets it as sig, and writes nothing unless the signed document verifies. Only the estate owner's key can do this.

Check it before publishing, against the out-of-band anchor and the last verified sequence: python3 tools/registry_sign.py verify --in ecosystem-spec.json --persisted-seq 2 --trust-anchor <estate_owner> must print 'verified: ok'.

Publish it at canonical_source through kody-w/rapp-map's own process. For registry_seq 2 that was one commit, 4c8ba6b, which changed ecosystem-spec.json and the public halves recorded in RAPP1_OWNER_ACTIONS.json together. rapp-map's gates require that: .github/scripts/standing-guard.mjs refuses a ledger whose owner_inputs disagree with the registry's bytes (registry_document_sha256), sig or registry_seq, and re-verifies the signature with verifyRegistry, which takes the owner from the document's own estate_owner entry; the check against the out-of-band anchor is the previous step.

risk: These are PUBLIC TEST KEYS. Anyone can re-derive each private key from its published label (vendor/rapp_hive2/sign.py test_key: Ed25519 seed = SHA-256 of 'rapp-hive/2:public-test-key/1\n' + 'contoso-model-hive/<slug>'). Registering them lets anyone sign new frames that the estate registry's verifier accepts for these six @contoso kids, at any utc a frame declares. A tombstone does not close this: frames declare their own utc, and at rapp-1@591e014 load_document refuses any registry holding a tombstone unless the consumer supplies trusted issuance context (tombstone_issued_at), which would affect every consumer of the estate registry. A deprecated spki entry verifies nothing.
if_declined: The model's signed frames stay unverified under RAPP/1 §10 by design, and the residual finding (38 x '§10 signature verification unavailable', status unverified, zero violations) should be recorded as accepted. Inside the Hive they still verify under rapp-hive/2 against the Hive's own identity records and anchor (python3 -B -m rapp_hive2 verify ../model/hive --anchor 03972c7e8049b59134681ef9b1d7af369e4b06273d262691c5b28d6c48dcdce8, from vendor/).
when_decided: Either way, a follow-up commit to this repository records the decision. It updates /status here and the status line of ANCHOR-REQUEST.md (for example 'declined on <date>; the residual finding is accepted' or 'registered at registry_seq <n> on <date>'). If the entries are registered, the same commit also updates /subject/finding here and the sentence in ANCHOR-REQUEST.md that no registry lists the signers.

related_gap.title: Hive members are names bound to keys, not RAPPIDs
related_gap.relation: Inside a Hive a member is a name bound to keys by the Hive's signed history, not a RAPPID in a registry. These six kids are exactly that; the spki entries would be 'a RAPPID linked where one is needed', and declining leaves them as G8 describes.
